A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H. Content can be matched across relocation and renumbering without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original latent-impact simulations, representation-learning evaluations, runtime/emissions measurements, and appendix ablation, NVAE, and transfer-learning results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports additional NVAE latent-impact measurements and revised CIFAR-10 evaluations in Appendix F.

M1.justification: Appendix F changes NVAE positive-view construction from resampling only the last code while fixing the first two to perturbing groups 2–3 while fixing group 1. The core InfoNCE minimax procedure and Continuous Sampling remain unchanged. Newly described GAN latent exclusions conflict with Appendix D's retained perturbations, so an actual GAN implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: The same image datasets, classification and detection tasks, transfer datasets, and efficiency scenarios remain. NVAE on CIFAR-10 already appeared in v1 Appendix F; its revised evaluations do not introduce a new dataset or input scenario.

E2.justification: The NVAE comparison adds real-data and unperturbed-synthetic-data controls in v2 Table 5, absent from v1 Table 4. Main GAN comparisons retain the same random and learned baselines, and the loader comparison retains PyTorch and FFCV.

E3.justification: Appendix F changes the NVAE random-baseline sweep from standard deviations 0.05/0.10/0.15 with truncation 2 to 0.2/0.3/0.4 with truncation 1, and introduces a multi-latent sweep of 0.3/0.4/0.5. It adds FID/IS evaluation and an NVAE latent-impact experiment. The classification table drops Top-5 reporting. Main benchmark splits and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 Appendix F adds a Monte Carlo analysis comparing NVAE latent-group influence and expands sensitivity testing of multi-latent perturbation magnitudes. The pixel-augmentation ablations, training-dynamics illustrations, and qualitative examples in the other appendices are retained.

E5.justification: The five-seed transfer evaluation, mean-plus/minus reporting, seed-handling instructions, and Monte Carlo mean/standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged. New NVAE statistics extend these reporting forms; no changed repeated-run count, significance test, or uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the transfer results, renumbered from Table 5 to Table 6, are unchanged. The NVAE classification results are replaced: v1's best ML result is 43.86% Top-1, while v2 reports 60.75%, alongside real and unperturbed-synthetic controls of 79.15% and 54.95%. Changed settings prevent interpreting this as a comparable performance gain. v2 also adds NVAE latent-impact results, FID 23.63, and IS 6.36 ± 0.16.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 adds Definition 2 and Equation (7), defining an implicit positive-view MI threshold through I(X1, X2) ≥ ρ. Existing minimax equations, the optimal-view proposition, and Appendix A mathematics remain unchanged; no new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The introduction now explicitly claims later-latent underutilization in 'all tested models,' whereas v1 describes it as occurring 'often.' This is a limited revision of the empirical claim's scope. MI-based quantification, synthetic positive-view generation, and Continuous Sampling remain the three headline contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds specific limitations concerning MI's invariance under invertible transformations, possible amplification of inherited biases through latent perturbations, and GPU/emissions costs when scaling Continuous Sampling. Appendix F also discusses the newly exposed accuracy gap between real-data and NVAE-based training.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a link advertised for this work's code and pre-trained models. Appendix F specifies 24 NVAE latent variables organized into three groups, where v1 described three scales/codes; this alone does not establish an architecture change. Appendix D additionally explains that the unused BigBiGAN latent remains perturbed for simplicity.

R1.justification: Section 3.2 replaces v1's characterization of SimCLR and Jahanian's tuning as violating the unknown-downstream-task assumption with an interpretation involving implicit MI thresholds selected through a pretext task. The cited-work set is retained; the Child and Serez reference updates are bibliographic corrections rather than new literature.

P1.justification: Substantial rewriting spans the abstract, introduction, related work, and methodological explanations, including material whose scientific content is retained. New explanatory subheadings and a reorganized account of perturbation selection alter the exposition beyond local copyediting. The limitations discussion and Appendix F are also expanded and rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adds an NVAE Monte Carlo table and restructures the NVAE classification table with additional rows and a single accuracy column. Tables 2–3 now share a page, several figures move, and captions clarify baseline attribution and change HL to ML terminology. Existing plots and qualitative image content are retained.

improvement.justification: The NVAE latent-impact analysis and added real/synthetic controls make the supporting evidence more informative, while code/model access information and specific methodological and scaling limitations improve transparency. These are limited gains: the main benchmark results are unchanged, and revised NVAE settings prevent a direct improvement claim. Inconsistencies between the main text's GAN latent exclusions and Appendix D, plus the NVAE prose's reference to an absent Top-5 column, temper the overall improvement.
